status: complete: two gear points per leveling level (the lab's standard gear and each level's best Forever set), raid, heal and tank values

spell_hit.note: Spell miss by the target's level minus yours (bosses +3). No 1% minimum miss: hit counts up to the whole miss chance and nothing above. Count talent and racial hit (the character's current spell hit). Leveling: the same-level row (4%); raids: 17%. Client tooltip CR_*_HIT_CAP_TOOLTIP.

melee_hit.note: Special attacks and a single weapon's swings; a dual-wielder's white swings miss 19 points more (27% vs bosses). Client tooltip: 8% melee/ranged and 27% dual wielding against raid bosses, 5% against your level.

expertise.note: Expertise lowers the target's dodge and parry alike: worth its value until dodge is gone (parry too when you stand in front, as solo leveling and tanking do).

defense.note: A boss crits a tank 5.6% at 300 defense skill, 0.04% less per point: 440 at 60. Below 60: 5 x level + 140 against a boss three levels up.

spell_penetration.note: Spell Piercing: past the target's resistance it is bonus damage, on average P / (P + 8 x your level + 19) of a spell's damage, a tenth on DoT ticks, none on Holy (wowsims/forever issue #76, 138 Forever combat logs). Leveling values from the fight lab (2026-11-13), raid values from the simulator.

haste.note: 10 rating = 1% faster casts and swings at every level. Whether haste shortens the global cooldown is open (the simulator says yes for spells, the client's Nature's Grace suggests no; _reference/forever-stats.md row 7).

not_scored.health_regen: not measured (the fight lab's eating time does not read health regeneration from gear)
not_scored.effects: Use, Equip-proc, chance-on-hit and set-bonus effects are not scored (static stats only); relics, idols, librams and totems with only an effect score 0 and say so

note: Class keys: the client's classFile, lowercased. Leveling: values are seconds per kill one point saves (fight lab), per level (every 5 from 10 to 60: interpolate; below 10 the level-10 numbers) and per gear point. Two gear points per level: 'standard' (the lab's standard gear) and 'best Forever set'; each carries item_stats, the set's summed item stats in these keys (hit and expertise left out). Place the character between them by its own items (preferred): share = delta(standard values, standard item_stats, your summed item stats without hit and expertise) / delta(standard values, standard item_stats, best item_stats), clamped 0-1, computed at each of the two levels around yours; values and seconds_per_kill = standard + share x (best - standard). Fallback: interpolate on the character's own total of the level's unit stat, clamped. Each level says caster (true: the spell hit cap; false: the melee cap). An item's gain = sum of (new - old) x value, its share of faster kills = gain / seconds_per_kill. Raid, heal and tank values: worth per point with the unit stat = 1 (1 Spell Power, attack power, healing power or Stamina); an item's share = its score change over the score of everything equipped. Spell lines map one to one: '+N Spell Power' -> spell_power, '+N Spell Damage' -> spell_damage, '+N Spell Healing' -> spell_healing, '+N Frost Spell Damage' -> frost_damage; count every line the tooltip lists (healing items list a third as a separate Spell Damage line). mp5 = the client's mana regeneration. Ratings per rating point, keyed by the stat keys (flat at every level). Hit counts only up to the cap (caps; the character's current hit with the replaced item's taken off): leveling hit_rating, raid hit_rating_below_cap. Rings and trinkets: the new item replaces the one that scores less. Values are clamped at 0. test_vectors: reproduce 'expected' within 'tolerance'. Models of the beta (fight lab, raid simulator, healer lab), not measurements.

raid.source: raid simulator, druid-balance.json (the spec's best build in its phase-1 BiS set, full raid)
raid.errors_note: one standard error of each value, same unit (raid simulator: the value's own stat-weights run repeated with its standard errors, raidsim/weight_errors.py, weight-errors.json: weights_stdev / sqrt(sample_counts) over the unit stat's weight). The unit stat carries its own error, not 0: with every error taken over the same weight, sqrt(sum ((new - old) x error)^2) over a swap's stats is the swap's error where it decides, at a gain of 0 (the ratio's scale error only rescales a gain, never its sign). hit_rating: the error of the value under the cap (the run with the set's hit taken off); a dual-wielder's is the larger of it and the BiS reading's (hit_rating_above_cap). Sum stats' errors as independent: over 12 seeds (weight-errors.json study) real slot swaps spread 0.8-1.1x that sum; per stat the errors are 0.6-1.3x the spread for crit, haste, hit, expertise and the main stats, and up to 1.8x low for spell power, attack power, strength and weapon DPS, whose errors are about 0.1% of their values. A gain inside about two errors is a tie

tank.source: raid simulator, feral-combat-ml-tank in feral-bear-tank, 2026-11-13: tank value per point (threat, damage taken, effective health)
tank.errors_note: one standard error of each value, same unit (raid simulator: tank_weights.py's stat-weights run repeated with its standard errors, raidsim/weight_errors.py, weight-errors.json): each stat's threat and damage-taken errors combined as tank_weights.py combines the weights (0.5 x / TPS, 0.25 x / DTPS, taken as independent; effective health is exact), over Stamina's share. Stamina carries its own error where the simulator weighed it; a stat with no key has none (the warrior's and the druid's Stamina: its share is effective health alone). spell_power: spell damage's and healing's errors together. Sum stats' errors as independent. Over 12 seeds (weight-errors.json study, the paladin) the shares spread 0.9x these errors overall; dodge, parry, block rating and defense about half of them (their threat and damage-taken readings move together), so those are conservative. A gain inside about two errors is a tie

The unit stat carries its own error, not 0: with every error taken over the same weight, sqrt(sum ((new - old) x error)^2) over a swap's stats is the swap's error where it decides, at a gain of 0 (the ratio's scale error only rescales a gain, never its sign). hit_rating: the error of the value under the cap (the run with the set's hit taken off); a dual-wielder's is the larger of it and the BiS reading's (hit_rating_above_cap). Sum stats' errors as independent: over 12 seeds (weight-errors.json study) real slot swaps spread 0.8-1.1x that sum; per stat the errors are 0.6-1.3x the spread for crit, haste, hit, expertise and the main stats, and up to 1.8x low for spell power, attack power, strength and weapon DPS, whose errors are about 0.1% of their values. A gain inside about two errors is a tie

tank.source: raid simulator, protection-ml-tank in prot-tank, 2026-11-13: tank value per point (threat, damage taken, effective health)
tank.errors_note: one standard error of each value, same unit (raid simulator: tank_weights.py's stat-weights run repeated with its standard errors, raidsim/weight_errors.py, weight-errors.json): each stat's threat and damage-taken errors combined as tank_weights.py combines the weights (0.5 x / TPS, 0.25 x / DTPS, taken as independent; effective health is exact), over Stamina's share. Stamina carries its own error where the simulator weighed it; a stat with no key has none (the warrior's and the druid's Stamina: its share is effective health alone). spell_power: spell damage's and healing's errors together. Sum stats' errors as independent. Over 12 seeds (weight-errors.json study, the paladin) the shares spread 0.9x these errors overall; dodge, parry, block rating and defense about half of them (their threat and damage-taken readings move together), so those are conservative. A gain inside about two errors is a tie

talent_note: Talents that change what a stat is worth, per class (talent_transforms: kind, per_rank percentages read from each rank's tooltip, stat / from / to / form). Each entry's values were measured with its own talents (leveling: levels.<L>.talents; raid, heal, tank: talents); re-state them for the player's own ranks before scoring. Per stat S: p = sum of S's stat_pct, c = S's convert fractions (S -> T); own = v[S] - (1 + p_build) x sum(c_build x v[T]); v'[S] = own x (1 + p_player) / (1 + p_build) + (1 + p_player) x sum(c_player x v[T]); Intellect's own part also x (1 + mana_player) / (1 + mana_build). Then v'[stamina] x (1 + health_player) / (1 + health_build), v'[armor] x armor ratio, v'[oh_weapon_dps] x off-hand ratio. A transform with form applies only to an entry whose forms list it. Fraction for rank k: per_rank[k - 1] / 100 (0 at rank 0; the last number above the table). Use v[T] as measured. Intellect's mana scaling applies whenever a mana_pct transform is live, with or without an Intellect stat_pct or convert. Clamp at 0 and round to 5 decimals only the values re-stated; every other value stays exactly as measured. talent_vectors: reproduce expected within tolerance (1e-5: expected is rounded to 5 decimals). A first-order re-statement, not a new measurement.
